new_task_1.title: Block coroutine and async-generator internals in the sandbox
new_task_1.description: The sandbox now classifies coroutine and async-generator frame/code attributes as internal so sandboxed templates cannot access those execution internals through attribute lookup on supported Python runtimes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure the sandbox treats coroutine and async-generator execution internals as unsafe attributes, matching the existing protection already applied to other callable and generator internals.

expectation.grounded: When sandbox attribute checks run against coroutine objects, access to `cr_frame` and `cr_code` must be considered internal and denied. When running on Python versions that define async-generator objects, access to their frame/code internals must likewise be considered internal and denied by sandbox attribute resolution.
expectation.conceptual: Sandboxed templates should not be able to introspect coroutine or async-generator execution state through special frame/code attributes. These objects should be protected the same way other internal Python execution objects already are.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to sandbox internal-attribute detection for coroutine and async-generator objects. It must not alter non-sandbox attribute access rules or broaden restrictions beyond the newly identified internal execution attributes.
constraints.conceptual: The update should tighten sandbox safety for execution internals without changing normal template behavior for ordinary, allowed attributes.

behavior: Sandbox internal-attribute checks must recognize coroutine objects and mark `cr_frame` and `cr_code` as unsafe.
On runtimes that expose async-generator types, sandbox internal-attribute checks must recognize async-generator objects and mark their frame/code internals as unsafe.
Sandboxed template attribute resolution must reject those internal coroutine and async-generator attributes instead of exposing them to template code.
Existing sandbox handling for other object types and non-internal attributes must remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a sandboxed template attempts to access `cr_frame` or `cr_code` on a coroutine object, the attribute must be treated as internal and not be exposed.

When a sandboxed template attempts to access the corresponding frame/code internals on an async-generator object in a runtime that supports that type, the attribute must be treated as internal and not be exposed.
When a sandboxed template accesses an attribute unrelated to these newly blocked coroutine or async-generator internals, existing sandbox behavior should remain unchanged.
